subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these food-product reviews and what's worth attention or actionable.

judge.implied_focus: Review value/attention-worthiness — which reviews merit attention based on their sentiment signal and community-perceived helpfulness/engagement

per_column.name: review_length
per_column.rationale: A generic textual metric, but plausibly a proxy for review substance/detail that feeds an attention-worthiness framing; weakly supportive rather than central.

per_column.name: sentiment
per_column.rationale: Categorical sentiment identifies the valence of feedback, directly relevant to 'what's worth attention' (e.g., surfacing negatives).

per_column.name: helpfulness_ratio
per_column.rationale: Normalizes the existing helpfulness numerator/denominator into a community-perceived usefulness signal — a strong facet of which reviews are worth attention.

per_column.name: has_criticism
per_column.rationale: Flags actionable negative content, directly aligned with 'actionable' reviews to investigate.

per_column.name: engagement_level
per_column.rationale: Buckets attention/engagement, a coherent facet of prioritizing reviews worth attention.

judge.rationale: The columns loosely orbit a single inferable focus — the attention-worthiness/value of a review — via helpfulness, sentiment, criticism, and engagement. However coherence is diluted: sentiment and has_criticism are largely redundant (both encode negative valence), and review_length is a bare mechanical text metric that does not cleanly join the focus. The set mixes an actionable value/prioritization theme (helpfulness_ratio, has_criticism, engagement_level) with generic NLP features (length, bare sentiment), so it is neither a tight facet decomposition nor pure noise. The implied focus is genuinely actionable — an analyst could triage low-helpfulness or critical reviews — but the framing is only partially realized because no column resolves what the reviews are actually ABOUT (topics/product aspects), leaving the 'what's in these reviews' half of the query unaddressed. Solid but not tightly centred.
